ABSTRACT

THE USE OF INSECTS AS BIO-INDICATORS OF WATER POLLUTION: A CASE OF EZE RIVER

Journal: Journal CleanWAS (JCleanWAS)

Author: Opoggen Lab, Emmanuel, C, Rotimi, J

This is an open access article distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License CC BY 4.0, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited

Doi: 10.26480/jcleanwas.01.2026.50.54

A baseline investigation was carried out on the aquatic insect community of Eze River, Onuiyi, Igbanke, Edo State, to determine the quality of the water body and aquatic fauna present, from April to July 2016. Three stations were selected and sampled; the physical and chemical parameters were investigated alongside aquatic fauna. The physical and chemical parameters were not significantly different (P > 0.05) for all the stations sampled throughout the sampling period. A total of 617 individuals belonging to 6 taxa were recorded, while bankroots had a total of 395 individuals in 6 taxa and sediments had 222 individuals in 4 taxa, which were Diptera, Odonata, Coleoptera, Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera. Of these, Diptera had the highest abundance all through the period of sampling, with the families Chironomidae and Ceratopogonidae having the highest occurrence, followed by the order Odonata, while Trichoptera had the least occurrence. The same number of taxa were recorded for all stations sampled; there was no significant difference between and within the insect groups (P > 0.05) for bankroot across all stations, while for sediment, there was a high significant difference between and within the groups of insects (P < 0.01) From the result of this study, Eze River has been found to contain negligible numbers of pollution-intolerant insects and therefore concluded to be polluted with organic matter.
